content: Ligand 1 is a methylthiophene butanamide on an aryl azetidine and ligand 2 a furylidene benzofuranone - both inactive, nothing to cross. Atom 0 is the thiophene methyl over an acyclic bond. Staying on the linker question: this episode reverses the amide. Every molecule I have built runs aryl-N(H)-C(=O)-cycloalkyl, with the donor on the ring and the acceptor pointing away. Flipping it to aryl-C(=O)-N(H)-cycloalkyl keeps the same atoms, the same molecular weight and the same number of donors and acceptors, but moves the N-H off the aromatic ring onto the aliphatic cap and puts the carbonyl in conjugation instead. I know a donor separated from its ring by a CH2 is worth less than a conjugated one - 0.07 against 0.10 - but that compared two amides in the same orientation, so it never tested the reversal itself. If the reversed amide holds up, what matters is having a donor-acceptor pair near that position at all; if it collapses, the anilide N-H is specifically required and the whole series is more constrained than I have been assuming. Surviving methyl goes to the pyridine C4. Expected product: about 281 Da.
